headline: Iran Asks UN to Condemn $20 Million US Bounty for Nuclear Info
content: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi asked the United Nations and its nuclear watchdog to denounce a US reward of as much as $20 million for information on Tehran’s nuclear program.The complaint comes after the State Department announced the reward — along with “possible relocation” — for specific details about Iran’s nuclear facilities and equipment, people associated with the program, including scientists, or their movements.President Donald Trump, who launched a war against Iran alongside Israel in late February, has openly spoken about again bombing Tehran’s nuclear facilities and has cited his intention to prevent the Islamic Republic from ever developing nuclear weapons as justification for the conflict. The US and Israel also conducted airstrikes on Iran’s nuclear program in June 2025.The US plea for information last week, which is under the government’s “rewards for justice” program, warned that Iran has enriched its uranium to 60% and that the International Atomic Energy Agency’s inability to monitor Tehran’s activities makes it difficult to know anything about the status of the programs.In a letter dated Tuesday, Araghchi urged UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the president of the UN Security Council and IAEA Director Rafael Mariano Grossi to condemn the offer and take steps to address what he described as threats to nuclear facilities and personnel.“Such an approach risks encouraging espionage activities and the targeting of nuclear scientists and technical personnel,” he wrote.The US and Israel killed much of Iran’s senior political and military leadership in the opening salvo of the current war, including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the head of the Revolutionary Guards and senior officials involved in the country’s nuclear and security programs. The latest conflict followed a 12-day war in June 2025 in which the US and Israel struck key Iranian nuclear facilities, which Trump claims “obliterated” Tehran’s nuclear program. Iran has since restricted IAEA access, leaving inspectors unable to verify the whereabouts of its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, or fully account for elements of its atomic program.For years, Iran has accused the US and Israel of targeting scientists linked to its nuclear program in an effort to impede its development. At least four Iranian scientists were killed between 2010 and 2012, while prominent nuclear scientist Mohsen Fakhrizadeh was assassinated near Tehran in 2020.Israel’s security service has a long history of conducting targeted killings, and after Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023 attack, Israeli forces bombed the militant group’s officials in Iran, Lebanon and in the Qatari capital Doha.©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Burnham Rejects EU Financial Rules Showing Brexit Reset’s Limits
content: (Bloomberg) -- Andy Burnham’s government won’t accept so-called dynamic alignment of the UK’s financial services rules with those of the European Union, a stance that raises questions about the premier’s wider ambitions for closer ties.Under the mechanism, the UK would automatically follow EU regulations in certain areas. But as ministers seek to maintain the City of London’s independence, the Burnham government does not want it to apply to financial services, UK officials told Bloomberg. The UK’s Labour government is in talks with the European Union to forge closer ties that may include alignment in sectors such as agriculture and energy, but British officials have told EU counterparts that applying it to financial services is a red line they’re unwilling to cross, people familiar with the matter said. All spoke on condition of anonymity because talks are ongoing.While the development will be welcomed by some in the City of London who have welcomed post-Brexit freedoms including the removal of a cap on bankers’ bonuses, it also highlights complications involved in Burnham’s push for a much closer EU relationship. If he were to try to take Britain back into the EU or join its single market, as he has said is possible, he would likely have to sign up to its rules governing financial services. A UK government spokesperson said it would not provide a commentary on its negotiations with the EU but stressed that Britain’s financial services were a key national strength. The UK’s opposition Conservatives and Reform UK parties have long opposed dynamic alignment, saying it would leave Britain as a rule-taker with no say over devising regulations.British banks took a hit after the UK voted to leave the bloc in 2016, but the divergence in regulations over the last decade means much of the sector now opposes alignment of its regulations.In July, TheCityUK, which represents Britain’s financial services industry, said automatic dynamic alignment “is not appropriate for the UK’s financial and related professional services industry.” It argued that the sector “requires the UK regulatory authorities’ speed of decision taking, flexibility and agility, and could not operate effectively under arrangements that require it to automatically follow the lead of another jurisdiction with different priorities and needs.”A paper published by UK Finance in June said “we do not support wholesale UK alignment or dynamic alignment with the EU in financial services,” arguing that Britain’s post-Brexit divergence meant it could now respond more swiftly to risks and market developments, and that its rules should be “tailored to domestic conditions.” The group argued that the UK had benefited from diverging from the EU on environmental, social and governance disclosures, digital assets and artificial intelligence.Burnham is maintaining the position held by his predecessor Keir Starmer’s government, which exempted financial services from a push for closer alignment with the EU, some of the people said. They said dynamic alignment on financial services was not included in a paper of common understanding agreed between Starmer’s administration and the EU in 2025. --With assistance from Laura Noonan.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
content:
Provides credit guarantee for loans extended under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana

Approval for corpus of Rs.5,000 crore facilitating PMMY loans amounting to Rs.12.6 lakh crore

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved thecontinuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) for a period of five years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme provides credit guarantee coverage to the Lending Institutions through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) against default risk.

As on September 2026, more than 60.36 crore loans amounting to Rs.43.34 lakhs crore have been sanctioned by lending institutions since launch of PM Mudra Scheme. CGFMU which was launched in January 2016 has acted as a major catalyst in enabling the growth of PMMY loans in the country.

• The purpose of the fund is to provide guarantee to Lending Institutions (LIs) for the following credit facilities:

• Loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) upto Rs.20 lakh;

• Overdraft of upto Rs.10,000 provided by banks under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts; and

• Loans granted to Self Help Group (SHG) where portfolio is between Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh.

headline: Haryana CEO dismisses misleading report on 2024 assembly poll figures
content: Chandigarh, Nov 11: The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Haryana, has termed a media report alleging discrepancies between votes polled and votes counted in 51 Assembly constituencies during the 2024 elections as misleading, stating that the actual polling figures were shared with candidates' polling agents and subsequently tallied with the votes recorded in Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).In a fact-check clarification issued on its official social media platforms, the CEO, Haryana, responded to a media report, which claimed that internal records of the Election Commission of India (ECI) showed mismatches between votes cast and votes counted in 51 seats across Maharashtra, Haryana, and Jammu and Kashmir.The report had specifically cited Badkhal and Kaithal constituencies in Haryana.The CEO said the actual figures of votes polled on polling day are shared with the polling agents of candidates through Form 17. These figures are then tallied with the figures recorded on EVMs at the time of counting."No complaints regarding differences in the figures of votes received from anyone in this regard. Reporters' Collective could have contacted us for any clarification," the CEO said.Citing the ECI's official index card for the Kaithal Assembly constituency, the CEO provided a breakdown of the total electorate and votes polled to counter the allegations.According to the index card, Kaithal had 2,23,449 registered electors, while the total number of votes polled through EVMs stood at 1,67,285. In addition, 1,566 valid postal votes were recorded, taking the total number of votes polled, including postal ballots, to 1,68,851.The CEO said the report had attempted to mislead readers by claiming that the ECI counted 1,67,070 more votes than were cast, whereas the actual number of votes polled, including postal ballots, was 1,68,851.The index card also recorded 512 votes deducted from EVM votes on account of test votes, rejected votes and other reasons, while 1,427 valid postal votes were counted. The total valid votes polled stood at 1,68,200.The CEO Haryana's clarification comes amid questions raised over discrepancies in election data and the accuracy of figures recorded during the 2024 Assembly polls. The authority maintained that the official polling records and the figures available on the ECI website provide the correct account of votes polled in the constituency. --IANS

headline: Russian paraglider trapped in power lines, rescued in Himachal
content: Shimla A Russian paraglider in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi, who got entangled in high-tension electricity wires over 100 metres above the ground, was rescued after a 3-hour-long operation on Tuesday (November 11, 2026), police said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/himachal-pradesh/ The incident occurred near Tandu, when Alexey (48) took off from Bir Billing and got stuck in the wires mid-flight. Following the incident, he immediately sent pictures of his location to the Bir Billing Paragliding Association to seek help. The association then alerted the district administration and dispatched rescue teams to the location. headline: Watch: Russian Paraglider Gets Stuck In High-Tension Wires 150 Metres Above Ground In Himachal, Rescued
content: A Russian paraglider pilot was left hanging from high-tension electricity wires, around 150 metres above the ground, in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district on November 10. He remained trapped for nearly two and a half hours before a rescue team managed to bring him down safely. The incident took place near Mehar village, about five kilometres from Mandi town, along the Pathankot-Mandi highway. Other paragliders in the area alerted the local administration after the pilot got caught in the power lines, leading to an urgent rescue effort. Officials Use A Hydraulic Crane To Reach The Pilot After receiving the alert, officials immediately switched off the electricity supply to avoid putting the pilot and rescue workers at further risk. Mandi Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) and police personnel also reached the spot to monitor the situation. However, rescuing the pilot was not easy because he was stuck at a height of around 150 metres. The administration arranged a 146-metre hydraulic crane to reach him. A State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) official then climbed into the crane’s basket and moved towards the stranded pilot. The official managed to bring him down safely after he had spent nearly two-and-a-half hours suspended from the wires. Meanwhile, people at the spot placed a tarpaulin and mattresses on the ground below him as a safety measure in case he fell during the operation. The Pathankot-Mandi highway was also closed to heavy vehicles while the crane was being set up and the rescue work was carried out. headline: NCS PROBATIONERS, 2025 BATCH, BHARAT DARSHAN IN MAHARASHTRA
content: The Nagaland Civil Services Probationers, Batch of 2025, commenced the Maharashtra leg of their Bharat Darshan on 1st November 2026, reporting to the Yashwantrao Chavan Academy of Development Administration (YASHADA), Pune. The five-day programme combined classroom interactions with institutional visits and cultural and heritage exposure, presenting a broad view of Maharashtra beyond its identity as India’s financial and industrial centre. The classroom sessions covered the functioning and policy priorities of the Maharashtra Government, including the Maharashtra industrial policy, startup ecosystem, ethical use of artificial intelligence, legal case studies and the environmental work of the 14 Trees Foundation. Discussions on land administration highlighted digitisation and easier access to land records. Initiatives associated with the MahaBhumi platform illustrated how technology can improve access, traceability and transparency in land-related services. Sessions with the Women and Child Development Department drew attention to support, care and rehabilitation for vulnerable women and children, including widows and orphaned children. The discussions underscored the importance of linking welfare delivery with protection, institutional and community-based care, rehabilitation and pathways to self-reliance. The probationers were also introduced to Maharashtra’s startup and entrepreneurship initiatives, including incubation, mentoring, seed-funding and innovation linkages that can help young enterprises access markets and finance. Field engagements included the Innovation Hub at the National Chemical Laboratory (NCL), an interaction at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Maharashtra, and a visit to the Pune Metro project to understand urban mobility and public transport infrastructure. At the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, the probationers were introduced to the institutional ecosystem supporting cinema, television and the creative arts. The programme also explored Maharashtra’s cultural and natural heritage. The visit to Asia Plateau, Panchgani, provided an opportunity to engage with its institutional and developmental setting. At Devrai Art Village, the probationers observed how local artisans work with materials such as metal and stone while experimenting with contemporary forms that draw upon traditional Indian artistic practices. The visit demonstrated the potential of craft-based livelihoods, design innovation and responsible tourism to support local communities. The field exposure to Mahabaleshwar included visits to Kate’s Point and Arthur’s Seat, offering an appreciation of the region’s distinctive topography and tourism potential. At MAPRO, the group observed the processing and marketing of locally associated food products, including jams, crushes, confectionery and chocolates. The visit illustrated how value addition, branding and visitor experiences can strengthen a regional tourism economy and create linkages for local producers. The group also visited Prabhat Studios, gaining an appreciation of the region’s film heritage.

headline: Chhattisgarh eases RTE admission norms to ensure 25% quota seats are filled
content: RAIPUR: In a policy shift, the Chhattisgarh government has overhauled admission guidelines under the Right to Education (RTE) Act to ensure that 25% of seats reserved for economically weaker and disadvantaged sections in private schools do not go vacant.Under the newly issued directives, the strict condition requiring students to live strictly within the school's immediate "neighbourhood limits" has been replaced with a tiered priority system.Previously, private schools often left reserved quota seats vacant by citing a lack of eligible applicants living within the prescribed local boundary. Under the revised framework, neighbourhood criteria will act strictly as an order of priority rather than a mandatory disqualification barrier.If an insufficient number of applications are received from within the designated zone, schools are now required to fill the remaining quota by admitting eligible children residing beyond the specified perimeter.Classes 1 to 5: First priority will be given to eligible children residing within a 0 to 1-km radius of the school.Classes 6 to 8: First priority will be accorded to students living within a 0 to 3-km radius.Unfilled/Vacant Seats: If seats remain unfilled after accommodating neighbourhood applicants, eligible students living beyond the 1 to 3-km limits will be admitted to ensure the full 25% quota is utilised..Chhattisgarh emerges as a national benchmark in digital governance of education.The new order eliminates bureaucratic delays by removing the mandate that previously forced schools and parents to seek individual permissions from competent authorities for every out-of-boundary admission. Along with easing red tape, the government has streamlined the fee reimbursement process under Sections 12(1)(c) and 12(2) of the RTE Act, ensuring private institutions receive timely, transparent state payments for admitted students.The reform stems from a January 2026 Supreme Court ruling characterising RTE admissions for underprivileged children as a vital national mission, followed by advisory guidelines issued by the Union Ministry of Education on October 21, 2026. headline: Press Statement of Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan issued from Shimla
content: He said that the people of Himachal Pradesh had endorsed the functioning, policies and guarantees of the Congress party in the 2022 Assembly elections, when a popular government led by Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu was formed with a massive mandate. He said that the people of Himachal Pradesh had once again endorsed the government's achievements, fulfilment of its guarantees, successful implementation of public welfare schemes and commitment to the overall development of all sections of society during the by-elections. "The BJP's humiliating defeat in the by-elections is a clear example that the people of Himachal Pradesh will never allow attempts to undermine the dignity of the Constitution, topple an elected government through political conspiracies or crush people's mandate through use of money power," he stated. Highlighting the state government's achievements over the past four years, he said that immediately after assuming office, Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu demonstrated the government's sensitivity towards vulnerable sections of society by laying the foundation of the Mukhya Mantri Sukh-Aashray Yojana. Under this scheme, approximately 6,000 orphaned and destitute children of the state have been adopted as 'Children of the State'. These children are now benefiting from free education, pocket money, festival allowances, exposure visits across the country, financial assistance to establish start-ups, land and financial support for house construction, along with several other facilities and provisions under the scheme. He said that in its very first Cabinet meeting, the Chief Minister restored the Old Pension Scheme for 1.36 lakh state government employees, thereby ensuring the financial security and future of employees and their families.

headline: 13th MTB Shimla 2026 Concludes Successfully, Celebrating Mountain Biking Excellence and Adventure Tourism in Himachal Pradesh
content: PNNShimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 11 :The 13th edition of MTB Shimla 2026 concluded successfully on October 25, 2026, in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, bringing together 72 mountain biking cyclists from 20 cities across India. Organised by the Himalayan Adventure Sports & Tourism Promotion Association (HASTPA), the three-day event celebrated competitive cycling, adventure sports and the growing mountain biking culture in India.The competition featured approximately 130 kilometres of challenging Himalayan routes, with around 3,800 metres of cumulative climbing and 3,500 metres of descent. The demanding terrain tested participants' endurance, technical abilities and determination across steep climbs, forest trails and challenging descents. Out of the 72 participating cyclists, 52 successfully completed the race.Atul Kumar Claims the Overall ChampionshipThe highlight of MTB Shimla 2026 was the impressive performance of Atul Kumar from Dharamshala, who secured the overall championship with a combined timing of 5 hours, 9 minutes and 25 seconds.Ayush Negi from Dehradun finished in second position with a timing of 5 hours, 14 minutes and 49 seconds, while Vansh Kalia from Shimla secured third place with a timing of 5 hours, 18 minutes and 5 seconds.The competition also recognised outstanding performances across different categories, highlighting the participation of both experienced athletes and emerging cyclists.In the Under-19 Boys category, Arnav from Chandigarh secured first place, followed by Puneet Thakur from Shimla and Arnav Chauhan from Dharamshala. In the Under-16 Boys category, Satvik Basta from Shimla claimed the top position, while Sneho Roy and Samaruth Rajesh from Bengaluru secured second and third positions, respectively.Mangal Singh from Hoshiarpur won the Masters Men category, followed by Gaurav Thakur from Solan and Roberto Bello from Delhi. In the Women's category, Aira Saran from Bengaluru secured first place, followed by Anupama from Gurugram and Anjali from Panchkula.The winners were recognised during the closing ceremony and prize distribution held on October 25.Three Days of Cycling Across the Himalayan TerrainThe event commenced on October 23 with a Heritage Ride from the historic Ridge in Shimla. Participants cycled through prominent locations, including Chaura Maidan, the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Summerhill and Vidhan Sabha, experiencing the city's heritage and surrounding landscapes.The subsequent competitive stages took riders through challenging mountain routes around Sanjauli, Dhalli, the Shimla Water Catchment Wildlife Sanctuary, Kufri, Mashobra, Charabra, Moolkoti, Sipur and Fagu.The routes featured demanding climbs, forest sections and technical descents that required riders to maintain focus, manage their energy and demonstrate strong cycling skills. The final stage concluded at the Ridge, marking the end of three days of competitive mountain biking.HASTPA's Contribution to India's Mountain Biking CommunityFounded in 2005, HASTPA has spent more than two decades promoting mountain biking and adventure sports in India. Through initiatives such as MTB Himalaya and MTB Shimla, the organisation has created opportunities for cyclists to participate in organised competitions, develop their abilities and gain valuable sporting experience.Its initiatives extend beyond competitive events and focus on grassroots talent development, youth participation, school engagement, cycling awareness and road safety. HASTPA also promotes helmet awareness and advocates the development of professionally planned cycling trails and supporting infrastructure.The successful completion of the 13th edition reflected the organisation's continued efforts to strengthen India's mountain biking ecosystem and encourage more young people to explore cycling as a sport.Strengthening Himachal Pradesh's Adventure Tourism PotentialMTB Shimla 2026 also highlighted Himachal Pradesh's potential as a destination for mountain biking and adventure tourism. By taking participants through forests, mountain trails, villages and scenic landscapes, the event showcased a different way of experiencing the Himalayan region.Such sporting events can support local economic activity by creating opportunities for accommodation providers, transport operators, guides, homestays and other tourism-related businesses. They also encourage visitors to explore destinations beyond conventional tourist attractions.HASTPA's broader vision includes developing quality cycling trails, encouraging safer roads, supporting young sporting talent and promoting sustainable adventure tourism across the Himalayan region.The conclusion of MTB Shimla 2026 marked another milestone in the organisation's journey of promoting mountain biking in India while bringing together sporting excellence, community participation and tourism development.About HASTPAThe Himalayan Adventure Sports & Tourism Promotion Association (HASTPA) is a non-profit organisation established in 2005. It is dedicated to promoting mountain biking, adventure sports, sustainable tourism and youth development in the Himalayan region. Through its flagship initiatives, MTB Himalaya and MTB Shimla, HASTPA continues to encourage cycling participation, support emerging athletes and showcase Himachal Pradesh as an adventure sports destination.Media Contact:Mohit SoodFounder & President, HASTPAMobile: +91 94180 45678Media Team: 8988000789, 9816569096(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by PNN. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: President Honours MC Theog; Himachal Pradesh shines in Swachh Survekshan
content: · MC Theog ranks among Top 20 Urban Local Bodies of the country · Vikramaditya Singh receives prestigious award from President Droupadi Murmu Under the visionary guidance and leadership of Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and state government's commitment to making Himachal Pradesh cleaner, greener and more sustainable, the state has achieved yet another milestone by securing a place among the Top 20 Urban Local Bodies in the country under Swachh Survekshan. Minister of Urban Development Vikramaditya Singh Neeraj Kumar received the award from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held in New Delhi today. The award holds special significance as, for the first time, the state's recognition has been conferred in the presence of the President. Vikramaditya Singh said that the state government has made concerted efforts to improve the overall performance of Urban Local Bodies under Swachh Survekshan. As a result of these focused initiatives, coordinated efforts and continuous monitoring by the government, Municipal Council Theog has been successful in bringing laurels to the state. He added that the achievement reflects the dedication and collective efforts of the Urban Development Department, Directorate of Urban Development, municipal authorities, sanitation workers and citizens. It also demonstrates the state government's commitment to strengthening urban sanitation infrastructure, improving waste management systems, ensuring public participation and promoting sustainable cleanliness practices.

headline: We will never forget. UNA honours and recognizes the sacrifices of all who have served this Remembrance Day
content: On November 11, we honour and remember the sacrifices of those who have served in the Armed Forces and continue to serve our country during times of war, conflict and peace. This commitment to never forget the sacrifices those who have paid the ultimate price in the service defence of our country is heavier this year following the accident that claimed the lives of four young Canadian soldiers at CFB Wainwright and injured dozens of others. Nurses, physicians, and health care workers at the Wainwright Health Centre, CFB Wainwright and hospitals around the province showed bravery and professionalism while providing care to everyone impacted by that terrible tragedy. Delegates to UNA’s Annual General Meeting have collected more than $13,000 in donations for the families of the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry soldiers injured or killed in the fire. UNA will match the total donations raised at the AGM by UNA members, and funds collected will be donated to support PPCLI families through a Canadian Army liaison. Wearing a red poppy is a visual pledge never to forget those who served and sacrificed. The red poppy is a powerful symbol of remembrance, sacrifice, and honour for all Canadians who have served and died in times of war and peace. Canadians from coast to coast wear red poppies during the lead-up to Remembrance Day, on November 11. The red poppy became an important symbol after the publication of "In Flanders Fields,” a poem written during the First World War by Canadian Lieutenant-colonel John McCrae after he presided over the funeral of a friend and fellow soldier. More than a century later, McCrae’s poem continues to poignantly express the tragedy of the losses of war, and the importance of carrying on their memories.

headline: NHAI opens 4.5 km Kangra Bypass stretch under Shimla-Mataur highway project for trial use
content: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has opened the 4.5 km Kangra Bypass stretch under Package V of the Shimla-Mataur four-laning project on NH-88 in Himachal Pradesh for public use on a trial basis. The bypass comprises a 593-metre twin-tube tunnel, three major bridges with a combined length of around 477 metres, a 160-metre viaduct, a 455-metre railway overbridge-cum-viaduct and a 155-metre bridge over Riyund Khad. Package VB covers the four-laning of an 18.13 km stretch from Bhangbar near Ranital to the Kangra Bypass, connecting with NH-154, at an estimated cost of Rs 9.9989 billion. The wider 36.4 km Jwalamukhi-Kangra section is being developed at a cost of Rs 12.8488 billion under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM). The Shimla-Mataur project covers 223.7 km of NH-88 in Himachal Pradesh.

headline: Russian paraglider hangs from high-tension wires 150m above ground for 2.5 hours in Himachal; rescued
content: MANDI: A Russian solo paragliding pilot was rescued after remaining suspended from high-tension power lines at a height of nearly 150 metres for over two-and-a-half hours in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district on Tuesday.The rescue operation was carried out near Mehad village, about 5km from Mandi town, where the local administration deployed a 146-metre crane to bring the pilot down safely.The pilot, identified as Evakin Alexei, had taken off from Billing in Kangra district before being swept off course by strong winds and getting entangled in power lines along the Pathankot-Mandi highway in the afternoon.“We were alerted by the locals and the power supply was immediately switched off,” an official said.Police and administration teams rushed to the spot alongside SDRF personnel and an NHAI worker, who used the crane’s basket to reach the stranded paraglider and lower him to safety.As a precautionary measure, bystanders spread tarpaulins and mattresses on the ground below. The Pathankot-Mandi highway was temporarily closed to heavy vehicles while the crane was assembled and the operation was executed.An official confirmed that although Alexei sustained no injuries, he was taken to the zonal hospital in Mandi for a routine medical examination.The incident highlights a recent spate of paragliding accidents in the region. On Nov 1, an Austrian pilot was injured after crashing into fields in the Gumma area of Jogindernagar sub-division in Mandi. headline: Pankaj Rai Appointed Chairperson of Himachal Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh government has appointed senior IAS officer Pankaj Rai as the new Chairperson of the Himachal Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (HPERC). The Energy Department issued a notification regarding his appointment late Tuesday evening. According to the notification, Rai will hold the position for a tenure of five years or until he attains the age of 65, whichever is earlier. Considered one of the experienced and capable administrative officers of the state, Pankaj Rai has held several important positions during his career. He has served as Deputy Commissioner of Bilaspur and Lahaul-Spiti districts, Commissioner of the Shimla Municipal Corporation and Mission Director of the National Health Mission. He has also served as Deputy Director (Administration) at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh. His appointment assumes significance as the selection process for the top post of the Electricity Regulatory Commission had remained under discussion for several months and was also challenged before the Himachal Pradesh High Court. On September 14, 2025, the selection committee had recommended a panel comprising IAS officers Pankaj Rai and Rajiv Sood for the post of Chairperson. However, the state government subsequently rejected the panel, prompting Pankaj Rai to approach the High Court against the decision. After hearing the petition, the High Court set aside the government’s decision to reject the selection committee’s recommendations and directed it to complete the appointment process in accordance with the panel submitted by the committee. The court had also fixed November 10, 2026, as the deadline for completing the appointment.

headline: Himachal: 16-member SDRF team rescues Russian paraglider trapped in power lines in Mandi
content: Mandi (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 11 (ANI): A Russian paraglider who got entangled in high-tension power transmission lines along the Mandi-Padder National Highway was successfully rescued in a coordinated operation by a 16-member State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) team, officials said on Tuesday.The high-risk rescue operation was executed with the assistance of the local administration, residents, and a 56-metre hydraulic crane.Following the rescue, the foreign national was shifted to a nearby hospital for medical evaluation and first aid.Sharing details of the operation, Vinod Thakur, In-charge of the SDRF Unit in Mandi, said specialised safety gear was deployed to ensure the paraglider's safe retrieval from the live transmission lines."We also deployed a belay safety system as a precautionary measure during the rope rescue operation. With the support of the local administration and residents, we successfully rescued the Russian national and shifted him to a hospital for first aid," Thakur said.Updating on the paraglider’s health status, the SDRF official added, "Prima facie, he appeared to be fine. He was conscious and able to speak. However, the doctors will be able to assess his exact medical condition after examination."Earlier, the Baddi Police have constituted special teams to arrest a man accused of opening fire on another person near the Lakad Depot on Ramshahar Road in Nalagarh on Tuesday.The victim, identified as Mohammad Aslam alias Ballu, sustained gunshot injuries in the incident.According to the police, the incident took place within the jurisdiction of Nalagarh Police Station. Aslam, son of Ghulam Rasool and a resident of Ward No. 7, Nalagarh, was rushed to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Nalagarh, for medical treatment. On the basis of a complaint lodged by Joginder Singh, son of Santokh Singh, a resident of village Pannar in Nalagarh tehsil, police registered a case under Sections 109 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 25, 54 and 59 of the Arms Act.As per the complaint, the accused, identified as Sahil, son of Rajender Singh and a resident of Nalagarh, allegedly fired multiple shots at Aslam before fleeing the spot on a motorcycle.Taking serious note of the incident, Baddi Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar (Vinod Dhiman, as mentioned in the press release) visited the crime scene and reviewed the situation. He also directed police officials to take immediate steps to apprehend the accused.Superintendent of Police Baddi Vinod Kumar said that "We have constituted multiple special police teams to ensure the early arrest of the accused. The teams are investigating all aspects of the incident and conducting searches at possible hideouts. Efforts are underway to apprehend the accused at the earliest."Police said that the investigation into the case was in progress and teams were pursuing various leads to trace and arrest the accused. (ANI)
